title: The Killer Shrews
note: A hurricane, a island lab and men in dog costumes; a beloved creature-feature disaster.

title: The Brain That Wouldn't Die
note: A surgeon keeps his fiancee's head alive on a tray; gloriously grisly drive-in horror.

title: Teenagers from Outer Space
note: Alien teenagers, a ray gun that turns people into skeletons, and a budget of about $20,000.

title: The Phantom Planet
note: A pilot shrinks and lands on an asteroid of tiny people; pure Saturday-matinee science fiction.

title: Attack of the Giant Leeches
note: Cajun swamp monsters and a very short running time; Corman-produced drive-in nonsense.

title: The Wasp Woman
note: A cosmetics queen injects herself with wasp enzymes; Corman's sharpest little horror.

title: A Bucket of Blood
note: Corman's beatnik-art satire: a busboy becomes a sculptor by encasing people in clay.

title: The Little Shop of Horrors
note: Corman shot it in two days, and the talking plant still works.

title: The Terror
note: Boris Karloff, a young Jack Nicholson and a haunted castle; made in three days on leftover sets.

title: Dementia 13
note: Francis Ford Coppola's first real film: an axe, a castle and a fortune.

title: White Zombie
note: Bela Lugosi as Murder Legendre, with the sugar-mill zombies that gave the genre its look.

title: The Ghoul
note: Karloff's first British horror, a resurrected Egyptologist and a stolen jewel.

title: The Old Dark House
note: James Whale's stormy-house comedy-horror with Karloff as the mute butler.

title: Dead Men Walk
note: A good doctor, an evil brother raised from the dead, and George Zucco in both roles.

title: The Vampire Bat
note: Fay Wray, Lionel Atwill and a village of vampires; German-expressionist sets on a poverty-row budget.

title: The Ape Man
note: Bela Lugosi turns himself into a gorilla to get his hair back; wonderfully deranged.

title: The Devil Bat
note: Lugosi breeds giant bats to kill his employers; the first of the cheap-and-glorious PRC horrors.

title: Bowery at Midnight
note: Lugosi as a soup-kitchen saint who is really a crime boss raising the dead.

title: The Corpse Vanishes
note: Lugosi harvests glands from brides; a Monogram quickie that became an MST3K classic.

title: Voodoo Man
note: Lugosi, George Zucco and John Carradine hypnotising women in the back of a gas station.

title: Invisible Ghost
note: Lugosi strangles people while hypnotised by his dead wife; his best Monogram part.

title: Things to Come
note: H.G. Wells' future history from 1940 to 2036, with design by the Bauhaus crowd.

title: Rocketship X-M
note: The first post-war Mars film, made in three weeks to beat Destination Moon to cinemas.

title: Flight to Mars
note: Cinecolor Mars, a crashed rocket and a surprisingly melancholy ending.

title: Kronos
note: A giant energy-eating robot lands in the desert; one of the smartest 1950s sci-fi pictures.

title: The Giant Gila Monster
note: A lizard, a hot rod and a small Texas town; drive-in cinema in its purest form.

title: Robot Monster
note: A gorilla suit with a diving helmet, and the line 'I will kill all humans'; unforgettable.

title: Cat-Women of the Moon
note: The first 3-D space film: dancers on the Moon and a very strange telepathy plot.

title: Santa Claus Conquers the Martians
note: Martians kidnap Santa; a Christmas cult film that has to be seen to be believed.

title: Manos: The Hands of Fate
note: Made on a bet, with a camera that could only film 32 seconds at a time; the summit of bad cinema.

title: The Beast of Yucca Flats
note: A nuclear blast turns Tor Johnson into a killer, narrated by a man who never appears on screen.

title: Eegah
note: A caveman in the California desert, Richard Kiel and Arch Hall Jr.'s guitar; sublime trash.

title: The Screaming Skull
note: A floating skull, a swamp and one of the great 1950s horror gimmicks.

title: I Bury the Living
note: A cemetery map where pushing pins kills people; a genuinely unsettling little film.

title: The Bat
note: Vincent Price, a mystery writer and a killer called The Bat; the old-dark-house film perfected.

title: The Hideous Sun Demon
note: A scientist who turns into a lizard whenever he is in sunlight; made by the man playing him.

title: Betty Boop: Minnie the Moocher
note: Cab Calloway sings 'Hi-de-ho' while a ghost walrus and dancing skeletons carry Betty through the Fleischers' best cartoon.

title: Betty Boop: Snow White
note: Cab Calloway's 'St. James Infirmary' over a jazz Snow White and a chorus line of skeletons.

title: Betty Boop for President
note: Betty runs for president in 1932, and the Depression-era jokes still land.

title: Betty Boop: Parade of the Wooden Soldiers
note: The toy-soldier parade that Disney later borrowed, animated with the Fleischers' rubbery grace.

title: Betty Boop: The Old Man of the Mountain
note: Cab Calloway's 'Minnie the Moocher' returns, with a mountain that sings back.

title: Betty Boop: I'll Be Glad When You're Dead
note: Calloway performs the title song while Betty fends off a jealous husband.

title: Betty Boop: Poor Cinderella
note: The only Betty Boop in colour: a two-strip Cinecolor fairytale with glass slippers and a pumpkin coach.

title: Betty Boop: Is My Palm Read
note: Betty's fortune told at a fairground, then a wonderfully surreal dream of ice floes and ghosts.

title: Betty Boop in Blunderland
note: Betty falls down the rabbit hole into a Fleischer Wonderland of talking animals and jazz.

title: Betty Boop and Grampy
note: Betty and Grampy throw a party with homemade instruments; the warmest cartoon in the series.

title: Betty Boop: Bamboo Isle
note: Betty dances with a rotoscoped live-action hula dancer, then survives a shipwreck.

title: Popeye: Ancient Fistory
note: Popeye in a fairy-tale spoof as a put-upon servant, with Bluto as the oafish prince.

title: Popeye: Big Bad Sinbad
note: Popeye and Bluto settle it in Sinbad's court, with spinach and a giant genie.

title: Popeye: Shuteye Popeye
note: A mouse invades Popeye's sleep; the quietest and funniest of the Famous Studios shorts.

title: Popeye: Private Eye Popeye
note: Popeye as a hard-boiled detective guarding Olive's diamonds from a very obvious thief.

title: Popeye: I Don't Scare
note: Popeye spends the night in a haunted house and refuses to admit he is terrified.

title: Popeye for President
note: Popeye and Bluto campaign against each other in a 1956 election-year gag fest.

title: Popeye: Patriotic Popeye
note: Popeye vs his nephews and a crate of fireworks on the Fourth of July.

title: Superman: The Mechanical Monsters
note: Flying robots rob Metropolis; the best of the Fleischer Superman shorts and a direct ancestor of Batman: The Animated Series.

title: Superman: Electric Earthquake
note: A mad scientist threatens to sink Manhattan, over painted backgrounds that look photographic.

title: Superman: Eleventh Hour
note: Wartime Superman sabotages a fleet by night; the most atmospheric of the seventeen shorts.

title: Superman: The Mad Scientist
note: The first Fleischer Superman: a death ray, the Daily Planet and a flying man in 1941.

title: Felix the Cat: The Goose That Laid the Golden Egg
note: Felix in a 1936 Van Beuren colour cartoon, chasing the goose and its golden eggs.

title: Flip the Frog: Fiddlesticks
note: Ub Iwerks' first sound cartoon, in two-strip colour: all rhythm, rubber limbs and barnyard noise.

title: Gabby: All's Well
note: The Fleischer Gabby short spun off from Gulliver's Travels, with a town crier who never stops talking.

title: Hector's Hectic Life
note: A dog tries to hide a litter of puppies from his landlady; a Noveltoon full of small perfect gags.

title: Jack Frost
note: Ub Iwerks' ComiColor fairytale, with a young Jack Frost painting the autumn leaves.

title: Little Audrey: Goofy Goofy Gander
note: Famous Studios' Little Audrey versus a goose, in bright primary-colour nonsense.

title: Little Lulu: Bargain Counter Attack
note: Lulu wrecks a department store; the best of the Famous Studios Little Lulu shorts.

title: Mighty Mouse: Wolf! Wolf!
note: Terrytoons' superhero mouse in a wolf-and-sheep parody, with a full operatic score.

title: Casper the Friendly Ghost: There's Good Boos Tonight
note: The very first Casper cartoon, and the source of his permanent melancholy.

title: Noveltoon: Naughty But Mice
note: Herman the mouse invents things he should not; a Noveltoon with real mechanical invention.

title: Noveltoon: The Stupidstitious Cat
note: Famous Studios' superstitious cat and Buzzy the Crow; a very 1940s gag machine.

title: The Cobweb Hotel
note: A spider runs a hotel for flies, with a neon sign and a trapdoor; the Fleischers at their strangest.

title: The Big Bad Wolf
note: The 1934 Little Red Riding Hood cartoon that Walt Disney sued over, and a gorgeous piece of animation.

title: The Talking Magpies
note: Heckle and Jeckle's debut: two bickering magpies and a very confused dog.

title: Woody Woodpecker: Pantry Panic
note: Woody Woodpecker's third cartoon, with a starving cat and the laugh that made him a star.

title: Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer
note: Max Fleischer's 1948 Rudolph, made for Montgomery Ward and the first film of the song.

title: Max Fleischer's Gulliver's Travels
note: The Fleischers' 1939 feature: the first American animated feature not made by Disney.

title: Namakura Gatana (The Dull Sword)
note: The oldest surviving Japanese animated film: a samurai buys a blunt sword and regrets it.

title: Momotaro: Umi no Shinpei (Momotaro, Sacred Sailors)
note: Japan's first animated feature, a wartime propaganda epic with genuinely beautiful animal animation.

title: Kumo to Churippu (The Spider and the Tulip)
note: A ladybird, a spider and a tulip; the most charming film the wartime Japanese industry made.

title: Ugokie Kori no Tatehiki
note: A fox and a badger transform into a temple full of monsters; the wildest pre-war Japanese cartoon.

title: Yoshichiro Salutes
note: Hakuzan Kimura's cut-paper animation, a rare survival from the 1930s Japanese avant-garde.

title: Mobile Suit Gundam, Episode 1
licence: official upload by GUNDAM CHANNEL INTL
note: Where it all starts: the colony attack, the Gundam standing up, and Amuro's bad day.

title: Mobile Suit Gundam 00, Season 1 Episode 1
licence: official upload by GUNDAM CHANNEL INTL
note: The 2007 reboot: four Gundams, a divided world and the best first episode of any Gundam.

title: Mobile Suit Gundam SEED Destiny, Episode 1 (English dub)
licence: official upload by GUNDAM CHANNEL INTL
note: The English dub of the sequel series, free and in full on the rights holder's channel.

title: Mobile Suit Gundam: The Movie I
licence: official upload by GUNDAM CHANNEL INTL
note: The first compilation film of the original series, in Japanese with subtitles.

title: Mobile Suit Gundam: The Movie II, Soldiers of Sorrow
licence: official upload by GUNDAM CHANNEL INTL
note: The middle film, and the bleakest stretch of the One Year War.

title: Mobile Suit Gundam: The Movie III, Encounters in Space
licence: official upload by GUNDAM CHANNEL INTL
note: The finale: A Baoa Qu, and the end of the One Year War.

title: Lupin the Third Part 4, Episode 7
licence: official upload by Anime! on TMS Official Channel
note: Lupin in Italy with a full English dub, from the studio that owns him.

title: Lupin the Third Part 4, Episode 6
licence: official upload by Anime! on TMS Official Channel
note: The other half of TMS's free Lupin sampler: Rebecca, Zenigata and a very Lupin wedding.

title: Robot Carnival (Full Anime Movie)
note: Eight animators, one anthology film, no dialogue; Katsuhiro Otomo's segment is worth the whole thing.

title: Digimon Adventure tri. 1: Reunion (Full Movie)
note: The grown-up Digimon reunion film, licensed and posted in full by its US distributor.

title: Digimon Adventure tri. 5: Coexistence (Full Movie)
note: The fifth film of the tri. series, free in full from the official licensor.

title: Digimon Adventure tri. 6: Future (Full Movie)
note: The finale of the tri. cycle, and the most emotional Digimon has ever been.

title: Big Buck Bunny
note: The Blender Foundation's second open movie: a rabbit, three rodents and a revenge plot, made to prove open tools work.

title: Sintel
note: A girl and a dragon, twelve minutes of genuinely moving animation with a full orchestral score.

title: Sprite Fright
note: Blender Studio's horror-comedy about mutant mushrooms and teenagers; their best-looking film.

title: Cosmos Laundromat: First Cycle
note: A suicidal sheep meets a salesman from another dimension; the pilot for a feature that never happened.

title: Caminandes 3: Llamigos
note: Koro the llama versus a penguin and a vending machine; silent slapstick, perfectly timed.

title: Caminandes 2: Gran Dillama
note: The llama tries to cross a fence; two and a half minutes of Chuck Jones-grade timing.

title: Glass Half
note: Two art critics argue about a glass of water; a sharp little comedy from the Blender Institute.

title: Coffee Run
note: A caffeine-fuelled chase through a city, animated in grease pencil over live action.

title: Tears of Steel
note: Blender's live-action/VFX hybrid, made to prove open tools could do a robot siege in Amsterdam.

title: Elephants Dream
note: The first Blender open movie: a machine world, two men and a telephone that goes nowhere.

title: Spring
note: A shepherd girl and her dog against the spirit of winter; the most beautiful film Blender Studio has made.

title: Charge
note: A one-take action short with a robot army and a very determined soldier.

title: Hero
note: A 2D open movie drawn entirely with Grease Pencil, about a girl and the hero in her sketchbook.

title: Agent 327: Operation Barbershop
note: A 1960s-style spy caper in an Amsterdam barbershop, from the Blender Studio team.

title: Wing It!
note: A test pilot, a faulty wing and a very stubborn bird; Blender Studio's comic short.

title: Duck and Cover
note: Bert the Turtle teaches 1950s schoolchildren to survive an atomic blast; the most-quoted civil-defence film ever made.

title: A Is for Atom
note: John Sutherland's Technicolor explainer, with a friendly cartoon atom and terrifying implications.

title: The House in the Middle
note: The US government's actual advice on nuclear survival: paint your house and mow the lawn.

title: Despotism
note: A 1946 warning on how democracies slide into tyranny, still shown in civics classes.

title: Master Hands
licence: public domain (published in the US before 1929)
note: A wordless 1936 ode to assembly-line labour, shot in a Chevrolet plant as if it were a ballet.

title: The Plow That Broke the Plains
note: Pare Lorentz's Dust Bowl documentary, with Virgil Thomson's score; the first great American government film.

title: The River
note: Lorentz's Mississippi flood film, the model for every American documentary that followed.

title: In the Suburbs
note: A 1957 sales pitch for the new suburban life, and an accidental time capsule of it.

title: A Date with Your Family
note: The most unintentionally funny etiquette film ever made: how to behave at dinner, in 1950.

title: To New Horizons
note: General Motors' Futurama, the 1939 World's Fair dream of an America rebuilt around the car.

title: The City
note: Lewis Mumford, Aaron Copland and a green argument against sprawl, made in 1939 and never bettered.

title: A Trip Down Market Street
licence: public domain (published in the US before 1929)
note: A camera on a San Francisco streetcar in 1906, four days before the earthquake levelled it.

title: Prelude to War (Why We Fight)
note: The first Why We Fight film: an Oscar-winning crash course in why America went to war.

title: The Nazis Strike (Why We Fight)
note: Capra's second Why We Fight, with animated maps that taught a generation geography.

title: Divide and Conquer (Why We Fight)
note: The fall of France, edited by Capra into something closer to a nightmare.

title: The Negro Soldier
note: The US Army's 1944 film for Black troops, a landmark of Black cinema made by the Army itself.

title: With the Marines at Tarawa
note: Oscar-winning combat footage from Tarawa, released to American audiences almost uncut.

title: Apollo 11: 16mm Onboard Film
note: The crew's own 16mm film from inside the spacecraft, with no narration and no music.

title: Fireplace 10 Hours (4K)
note: Ten hours of a real fireplace in 4K, no loops, no music.

title: Cozy Fireplace 4K, 10 Hours
licence: official upload by Cozy Fireplace Space
note: A stone hearth, crackling logs and a dark room; the classic winter background.

title: Fireplace Evenings of Calm
note: Twelve hours of burning logs with a quieter, slower fire than most fireplace videos.

title: 10 Hours of Gentle Rain on a Window
licence: official upload by The Relaxed Guy
note: Rain on glass against a black screen; nothing else happens, which is the point.

title: Rain on a Window with Thunder
licence: official upload by Relaxing Ambience ASMR
note: Eight hours of heavy rain and distant thunder, recorded in one take.

title: Rain on the Window: 10 Hours
note: Eleven hours of gentle rain, mixed to sit under conversation or sleep.

title: Sea Otter Cam, Vancouver Aquarium
note: Live sea otters floating on their backs; the least stressful live stream on the internet.

title: Kelp Cam and Carry On
licence: official upload by Monterey Bay Aquarium
note: Five hours of the kelp forest tank, with the fish traffic and the light moving through.

title: 7 Hours of Ocean Waves at Sunrise
licence: official upload by Dive into Tranquility: Relaxing Ocean Waves
note: A single sunrise over the sea, seven hours long, no music.

title: 10 Hours of Huge Waves
licence: official upload by Relax Night and Day - Beautiful Nature & Sounds
note: Big surf and grey skies for ten hours; good for drowning out an office.

title: Snowstorm, Blizzard and Howling Winds, 10 Hours
licence: official upload by Relax Night and Day - Beautiful Nature & Sounds
note: A white-out blizzard with wind, ten hours of it.

title: Ambient Underwater 4K, 12 Hours
licence: official upload by Nature Relaxation Films
note: Twelve hours of slow underwater footage with no music; the most calming thing in the catalogue.

title: 8 Hours of Beautiful Birds (No Music)
licence: official upload by Nature Relaxation Films
note: A feeder in a garden for eight hours, with real birdsong and no soundtrack.

title: The World's Waterfalls in 4K (No Music)
licence: official upload by Nature Relaxation Films
note: An hour of waterfalls from five continents, with nothing but the water.
